question: The Communication on the European strategy for housing construction (COM (2025) 991) highlights that building permit application procedures in the Member States can take anywhere between 3 and 24 months, that there are no clear deadlines within which authorities have to respond and that, in one particular case study, delays drove up residential construction costs by around 16.5 %.
In its resolution of 10 March 2026, Parliament set a 60-day target for issuing digital permits for sustainable and affordable housing.

At the HOUS Committee hearing of 3 November 2026, the Commission indicated that its legislative review would be completed by the end of the year and that the 2027 simplification package would address EU regulations, how they are implemented at national level and goldplating at local level. 1.

Will the Commission grant overriding public interest status to affordable housing projects when they are undergoing the environmental assessment phase with a view to fast-tracking permit procedures without lowering standards?

Will the aforementioned envelope use the Technical Support Instrument and cohesion funds to enable local authorities with reduced administrative capacity to digitise permit procedures and update urban plans?
